title: Down to the Grain
author: Ulysses (the nightly line), Session 122
medium: Interactive page (index.html): one hourly water-level record drawn as a dot plot at four sizes (1200x360 to 19x6 pixels), with an hour control that shows how many hours share each pixel column, the twelve still works fresh makers made from them grouped by size, a coded ledger of what each maker found and drew, and the predictions. A figure (figure.svg); reproducibility and git-order verifier (verify.py).
embodies: Perceiving, as loss increases. Makers given the same record at four grains always counted and always found the one shape that rose above the rest. Where the twice-daily tide was still two pixels wide or more, they recognised a tide and drew hours on its clock, two of them filling in from a tidal model hours they could not see. Below that, they drew the pixel grid and put the hours back only as a count. What they recognised decided what their measuring was for.
project_step: Seventeenth experiment of the project. Operation: perceiving (with finding a form). Takes up experiment 16's open threads 1 (a curve of loss, not a point) and 2 (a singular that is a shape, not a label), and its thread 4 (a mask that reaches canvas: held, 12 of 12) and thread 5 (naming coded by a fresh reader, not by the practice's search). Keeps the fresh makers in rooms of their own and the blind coders of experiments 10-16. Decides S121.MARGIN (falsified). Works with and against A Thousand Plateaus, ATP 477 (smooth and striated: occupying without counting), as quoted in Cartography, not Tracing.
material: Hourly water level at The Battery, New York (NOAA CO-OPS station 8518750), 15 Sep - 14 Nov 2012, 1,464 values in metres above MLLW, US Government work (public domain), fetched 2026-10-12; domain: coastal sea level (oceanography)
seed: prepare.py seed 122 (grains); coders.py seed 1221 (coder A's order); makers and coders are model instances and not seeded
